daily_brief: Tensions in the Middle East remain elevated as Iran issued sweeping new conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, demanding US compensation, troop withdrawal, and an end to sanctions before restoring full shipping access [BBC], [France 24], [Al Jazeera], [Globe and Mail]. Within the EU, a diplomatic row between Spain and Italy intensified as both countries imposed reciprocal border checks following the unprecedented influx of over 70,000 migrants into Spain's Ceuta enclave from Morocco [BBC Europe], [The Guardian], [France 24], [RFI], [Globe and Mail]. In the United States, Todd Blanche was narrowly confirmed as Attorney General in a 50-49 Senate vote, with two Republican senators joining Democrats in opposition over concerns about his handling of Epstein documents and Trump's controversial 'anti-weaponisation' fund [BBC World]. Ukraine's President Zelensky warned from Belgrade that Russian strikes have left the country with virtually no intact thermal power plants ahead of winter [France 24]. Meanwhile, German authorities are investigating a drone loaded with explosives discovered at Leipzig airport near Ukrainian cargo planes, with officials warning of a 'new level of danger' potentially involving foreign powers [BBC Europe], [RNZ].

top_stories.headline: Iran Sets Sweeping New Conditions for Strait of Hormuz Reopening, Complicating US Talks
bullets: Iran's Supreme National Security Council stated the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US 'corrects its behaviour,' issuing six conditions including compensation for war damages, lifting of sanctions, withdrawal of US forces, and release of frozen assets
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said talks with Oman were 'approaching final stages' but reopening remains 'subject to other conditions' beyond the bilateral deal
Oman's foreign ministry reported positive discussions but warned against attacks on shipping that could hamper negotiations; the UAE reported one of its ships was targeted by an Iranian missile
The strait has been effectively blockaded since February when US-Israel military operations against Iran began; roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas typically transits the waterway

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Focused on diplomatic progress with Oman while noting Iran's caveats

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Emphasized complexity of demands and quoted conditions in detail via liveblog format

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Highlighted IRGC statement and framed conditions as separate from Oman negotiations

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Included UAE ship targeting and broader regional context including Turkey-Kurdish developments

top_stories.headline: Spain and Italy Impose Reciprocal Border Checks as Ceuta Migration Crisis Escalates EU Tensions
bullets: Spain began temporary border checks on travellers from Italy at midnight Saturday, set to last until September 7, in response to Italy's similar measures imposed on August 1
Italy introduced one-month border controls after approximately 78,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta on July 30-31, with more than 80 deaths reported
Spain's Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares called Italy's measures 'a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity' and 'discriminatory for the Spanish population'
Italy's government under PM Giorgia Meloni refused Spain's deadline to lift restrictions, stating controls would remain at least until August 15 when Spain 'expects a new wave of migration'

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Neutral presentation emphasizing both sides' positions and practical implementation details

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Spanish criticism of Italian measures and EU unity concerns

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Included tourist reaction and described it as escalation between EU partners

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Highlighted 'migration showdown' framing and quoted Spanish characterization of measures

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Provided fuller context on death toll and noted most migrants have returned to Morocco

top_stories.headline: Trump's Former Lawyer Todd Blanche Confirmed as US Attorney General in Narrow 50-49 Vote
bullets: Todd Blanche, who served as Trump's personal defence lawyer, was confirmed as Attorney General after serving as acting AG since April
Two Republican senators, Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski, joined all Democrats in opposing the nomination; Senator Bill Cassidy cast the deciding vote
Republican concerns centered on Blanche's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related document releases and his role establishing Trump's $1.8 billion 'anti-weaponisation' fund
Blanche pledged during confirmation hearings to walk back the fund, which critics feared would compensate January 6 participants, though it remains unclear if the commitment is legally binding

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the lengthy standoff and bipartisan opposition, noting uncertainty about whether Blanche's pledges are binding

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Faces Winter Without Working Thermal Power Plants After Russian Strikes, Zelensky Warns
bullets: President Zelensky stated during a visit to Belgrade that Ukraine has 'virtually no intact thermal power plants' as it prepares for the heating season
Overnight Russian strikes killed four people including a three-year-old child in the Kyiv region; 13 deaths total were reported from strikes and frontline shelling in 24 hours
The visit marked Zelensky's first official trip to Belgrade, where he met with Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic
Both Ukraine and Russia have been escalating long-range strikes, causing growing civilian casualties more than four years into Russia's large-scale offensive

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Focused on energy infrastructure vulnerability and civilian toll, noting this was Zelensky's first official Belgrade visit

top_stories.headline: Germany Investigates Explosive-Laden Drone at Leipzig Airport Amid Hybrid War Concerns
bullets: An explosive-equipped quadcopter drone was discovered on a runway at Leipzig-Halle airport late Tuesday near Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes marked with Ukrainian national colours
German Interior Minister warned of a 'new level of danger' from an attack that 'may involve foreign powers'; federal prosecutors launched a probe into threats to foreign and domestic security
A DHL cargo plane collided with an unidentified object during a go-around, sustaining slight damage; investigators believe it may have been a second drone
Russia's embassy in Berlin dismissed the incident as a 'fabricated provocation' and criticized 'anti-Russian hysteria,' though German officials have not publicly attributed blame

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Detailed technical investigation while noting Russia's denial and previous 2024 plot involving Russian-linked proxies

sources.name: RNZ
sources.framing_note: Led with Russia's denial and embassy statement, framing it as accusation without evidence
